title: Canteen coupons: who did not order in November?

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own canteen story, tables, datasets, queries and editorial; no text from any problem site.

stem:
Annapurna canteen runs a pre-order app for the students of a college. At the end of each month the mess committee sends a "we miss you" coupon to every student who placed **no app order in that month**.

**Tables**

`students`

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `student_id` | INTEGER, primary key | |
| `name` | TEXT, not null | Names can repeat |
| `hostel` | TEXT | NULL for a day scholar |

`orders`

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `order_id` | INTEGER, primary key | |
| `student_id` | INTEGER | The student who ordered; **NULL for a walk-in counter sale**, which belongs to no student |
| `item` | TEXT, not null | |
| `amount` | INTEGER, not null | Rupees |
| `ordered_on` | TEXT, not null | ISO date, `'2026-11-17'` |

**Task:** return `student_id` and `name` of every student with no order dated in November 2026 (`2026-11-01` to `2026-11-30`, both included). Orders in other months do not count. Sort by `student_id` ascending. If every student ordered in November, return no rows.

wrong.why: NOT IN against a subquery that can return NULL (a walk-in order) is never true, so no student is returned.
The date filter sits in WHERE after the join: a student with an October and a November order is kept, and a student with two October orders shows twice.
Checks only the month number, so a November 2025 order wrongly counts as November 2026.

starter:
-- Students with no app order in November 2026.
-- Columns: student_id, name; sorted by student_id.
SELECT student_id, name
FROM students;
hints: Start from students, not orders: the students we want are the ones with nothing on the orders side.
A LEFT JOIN keeps every student, and the order columns come back NULL when nothing matches. Which clause should decide what a November match is?
Put the date range in the ON clause and keep the rows where o.order_id IS NULL. Avoid NOT IN on a column that can hold NULL.

approaches.name: LEFT JOIN + IS NULL
approaches.summary: Join each student to their November orders only (the date range in ON) and keep students whose order_id stayed NULL.

approaches.name: NOT EXISTS
approaches.summary: Keep a student when no November order with their id exists. Safe with NULLs, and reads like the task.

approaches.name: EXCEPT
approaches.summary: All students minus the students who have a November order. Short, and fine here because student_id is a key.

revision_card.front: Find rows with no match in another table (an anti-join). What are the safe patterns, and what is the trap?
revision_card.back: LEFT JOIN with the match conditions in ON, then WHERE right.pk IS NULL; or NOT EXISTS. Trap: NOT IN (subquery) returns nothing if the subquery yields a NULL. Filters on the right table go in ON, not WHERE.
